title: Local Automorphism-Aware Syndrome Compilation for General Quantum LDPC Codes
authors: Eugenio Durazo Rocha, Olai Å. Mostad, Hsuan-Yin Lin, Eirik Rosnes
abstract: Low-depth syndrome extraction for Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) quantum low-density parity-check codes can be formulated as a proper ordered edge-coloring problem subject to quantum parity constraints. A proper edge-coloring of the CSS Tanner graph ensures that each data or ancilla qubit participates in at most one two-qubit gate per layer, but does not guarantee a valid interleaving of the X- and Z-check measurements as for every overlapping X/Z check pair, the number of shared data qubits on which the X interaction precedes the Z interaction must be even. The minimum number of colors in a proper ordered edge-coloring satisfying the quantum parity constraints equals the minimum two-qubit depth when each stabilizer check is measured with a single ancilla.   We introduce local automorphism-aware syndrome compilation (LocalASC), which reduces the constraint system to edge-orbit variables under a subgroup of the Tanner graph automorphisms and lifts each feasible orbit assignment to the full graph. Although the $6$-layer degree lower bound is unattainable for the published weight-$6$ IBM bivariate bicycle codes, we show that this is not universal among two-block CSS codes. Among code instances for which the maximum check weight equals the maximum Tanner graph degree, LocalASC finds depth-optimal syndrome-extraction schedules for several two-block CSS codes with odd component weights, including instances with unequal odd weights. We also obtain lower-bound-saturating syndrome-extraction schedules for several quantum Tanner codes satisfying the same degree condition. To obtain the subgroups used by LocalASC without computing the full automorphism group of the Tanner graph, we construct translation subgroups for two-block group-algebra CSS codes over abelian groups. For quantum Tanner codes, we give conditions under which square-complex symmetries extend to Tanner graph automorphisms.
summary: This paper introduces Local Automorphism-Aware Syndrome Compilation (LocalASC) to optimize the circuit depth required for syndrome extraction in quantum LDPC codes. By exploiting the symmetries (automorphisms) of the code's Tanner graph, LocalASC simplifies the complex scheduling constraints. This leads to the discovery of depth-optimal and lower-error-rate syndrome extraction schedules compared to prior state-of-the-art methods.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of finding low-depth syndrome extraction circuits for general quantum LDPC codes.
main_result: The proposed Local Automorphism-Aware Syndrome Compilation (LocalASC) method successfully finds depth-optimal syndrome-extraction schedules for several tested quantum codes, often outperforming existing compilation techniques.
method: LocalASC reduces the complex quantum-constrained edge coloring problem to edge-orbit variables by leveraging subgroups of the Tanner graph's automorphisms, simplifying the constraint system.
model_or_system: The work analyzes Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) quantum LDPC codes, which are modeled using their associated Tanner graphs, incorporating constraints from X- and Z-check measurements.
key_observables: Minimum two-qubit depth ($\lambda_{	ext{SEC}}^{\star}$), Logical Error Rate (LER), and Circuit Distance ($d_{circ}$).
important_parameters: The maximum degree of the Tanner graph ($\Delta(G)$) serves as a key lower bound for the required depth.
main_assumptions: The method assumes the existence of appropriate automorphism subgroups ($H \leq 	ext{Aut}(G)$) to simplify the constraint system.
figures_summary: Figures compare the performance (e.g., LER) of LocalASC against other scheduling methods for specific codes like [[48, 4, 8]] and [[72, 12, 6]], demonstrating superior performance.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem as a quantum-constrained edge coloring problem, introduces LocalASC by reducing constraints to edge orbits, and then validates its effectiveness by comparing its results against established methods and analyzing specific code families.
why_interesting: While focused on quantum error correction, the underlying mathematical machinery involving graph automorphisms, constraint satisfaction, and optimization techniques is highly relevant to designing efficient quantum circuits for any complex quantum system.

figures.caption: Fig. 1. The standard CSS Tanner graph of the [[6, 2, 2]] code in Example 1. Solid and dashed edges are incident on X- and Z-check vertices, respectively.

Fig. 2. A quantum-valid 4-edge coloring of the CSS Tanner graph in Fig. 1. Solid and dashed edges represent CX and CZ gates, respectively. Each color class is a perfect matching of size 6, and ηij(t) = 0 for every overlapping X/Z check pair.

Fig. 3. The order-3 LocalASC reduction for the [[6, 2, 2]] code. The 8 saturated edges are orbit representatives and correspond to the tick variables of the orbit model. The remaining 16 edges are shown faintly, since all edges in the same orbit receive the same tick. Each monochromatic orbit contains 3 edges.

Fig. 3 shows the corresponding orbit representation. Solving for one tick variable per orbit and lifting the resulting as- signment recovers the coloring in Fig. 2. Each of the 8 orbit variables determines the common tick assigned to the 3 Tanner edges in its orbit. Each color class in Fig. 2 is a perfect matching, and Example 2 verifies (C3) for all 9 overlapping check pairs. Therefore, the lifted coloring is quantum-valid.
Fig. 4. LocalASC filtering with 50 steps for the [[48, 4, 8]] coset-based code with fixed seed for noise in memory at physical noise level p = 0.001.
